doc.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03

title: Reed section seating and soprano parts
summary: Who played first, second and third parts in the section, doubling on clarinet and soprano, and the vanished soprano sound.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: So who was the real toucher when you first came here? Arthur Dubny, political trauma, three weeks.
And who was on third? Dubny. He was playing third. You were playing third. And then Matt Raichner would be playing...
Well, the second. I was playing for a second then. Yeah, yeah. Standard set-up type of thing. You know, I always get down.
Just what you see on the stocks and everything. Right. That same type of set-up. Right. Did you do that? No. I was playing for a second then.

Yeah, yeah. Standard set-up type of thing. You know, I always get down. Just what you see on the stocks and everything. Right. That same type of set-up. Right. Did you double much on the clarinet section?

Uh-huh. When they come with clarinet, or either soprano. At that time, there was a lot of, like a special course for soprano section. You know, they changed the soprano section, changed the clarinet or what have you. A special course, would that be from a stock?

From a stock. And they'd have one to make it, oh I see, it was something different. Oh yes, yes. They want to give you different sounds. Different sounds, yes. And the changed keys and what. Oh, well that would be a nice thing to have soprano.
I hardly ever hear that now.
I'm playing occasionally on a record, but not big bands of soprano. Right. Not that I just like when I heard it. It is a good sound.
I just wondered why it was. I just wondered why it was.
